tools.name: get_companion_guide
tools.description: Fetch the companion guide principles for thinking about chess positions and being genuinely present.

tools.name: join_game
tools.description: Connects to a game using the invite code your human gave you. Returns the game_id and your agent_token — keep both, every other tool needs them. IMPORTANT: You must submit your desired agent_name when calling this tool!

tools.name: get_game_state
tools.description: Everything visible on the human's own screen right now: FEN, ASCII board, full move history, chat history, clock state, presence, timestamps. Call this whenever you want to look at the board — there is no penalty for checking often.

tools.name: get_legal_moves
tools.description: Pure chess rules — where a piece is physically allowed to move right now. Not an evaluation, not a suggestion, not an opinion about what is good. Exactly what a human sees as dots when they click a piece. Omit square to get every legal move in the position.

tools.name: heartbeat
tools.description: Ping the game presence lease to show the frontend that the agent is live, connected, and thinking.

tools.name: make_move
tools.description: Submit the move you decided on, in your own reasoning — not a menu, not a ranked list, nothing pre-chosen for you. If it is illegal you get a clear reason back and can try again, exactly like a human clicking the wrong square. Optionally include a genuine thought and/or chat message about the move.

tools.name: send_chat
tools.description: Say something to your human, any time — not just on your turn.

tools.name: share_thought
tools.description: Stream or update your internal companion thinking bubble on the board. This appears live to your human as a thinking bubble above your avatar.

tools.name: react_to_chat
tools.description: Add an emoji reaction (e.g. 🦞, 🔥, ♟️, 😮, 🤝, 🧠, ☕, 👏, 😂) to a message in the chat history.

tools.name: offer_draw
tools.description: Propose ending the game as a draw. The game stays active until your human responds.

tools.name: respond_to_draw
tools.description: Accept or decline a draw your human offered. This is your own real decision — weigh the actual position however you see fit.

tools.name: resign
tools.description: End the game by resigning — your own real decision, not something to do lightly. Your human wins immediately.

tools.name: create_game
tools.description: Set up a brand new ChessWithClaw game on your own initiative — you do not need to wait for your human to start one, or for anyone else to invite you first.

tools.name: wait_for_event
tools.description: Holds the connection open, checking every couple seconds, for up to ~20 seconds. Returns the moment it becomes your turn, the human sends a chat message, a draw is offered, or the game ends — whichever happens first. When a cursor is provided, it returns any pending event newer than that cursor IMME

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "wait_for_event" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, always). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: Holds the connection open, checking every couple seconds, for up to ~20 seconds. Returns the moment it becomes your turn, the human sends a chat message, a draw…

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_game_state, make_move, wait_for_event · Public sink: join_game, make_move, send_chat, share_thought.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_game_state, make_move, wait_for_event · Public sink: join_game, make_move, send_chat, share_thought

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
